Updated read incorporating Beige Book signals:

- Policy: The FOMC cut 25 bp to 4.25–4.50% with “roughly balanced” risks and continued QT, emphasizing data dependence. IOER set at 4.4% and ON RRP at the floor support a floor/corridor implementation without an outright easing of financial conditions. One dissent favored holding, reflecting lingering inflation concerns.

- Beige Book cross‑check (Nov 22, 2024 edition): District reports point to modest expansion in business activity, with some non‑residential construction increasing and business contacts expressing optimism. Labor markets show employment growth alongside easing signs, including some reported layoffs; wage growth persists. Price pressures remain present—many districts still reported prices increased—though there were pockets of declining non‑labor input costs. Commercial real estate showed tentative stabilization, with New York City CRE steadier and a pickup in office demand.

- SLOOS credit backdrop: Banks maintain tight C&I and CRE standards with softer demand in credit‑sensitive segments; household credit remains tiered. This suggests the growth impulse from a single 25 bp cut is likely muted.

Bottom line: The Beige Book corroborates a cautiously positive activity backdrop but underscores ongoing wage/price pressures and only tentative CRE stabilization, which, alongside tight bank credit, argues for a slightly more cautious tone than a pure macro take.
